records.context: 1.  Gene ids are parsed in one place. ``TGGT1_224750``, ``gene_fraction:gene[224750]`` and the guide ``224750_2`` are all gene ``224750``, as determined by :func:`spacr.annotation.gene_number`; a second parser could make the volcano and the hit list name different genes.

records.translation: 1.  Los identificadores de gen se analizan en un solo lugar. ``TGGT1_224750``, ``gene_fraction:gene[224750]`` y la guía ``224750_2`` son todos el gen ``224750``, según determina :func:`spacr.annotation.gene_number`; un segundo analizador podría hacer que el gráfico de volcán y la lista de aciertos nombraran genes distintos.

records.context: 2.  Missing annotation is reported as text. A gene with no annotation row gets :attr:`GeneFacts.reason` -- "no row in the bundled Toxoplasma annotation" -- rather than a block of empty fields, which would read as "measured, found nothing". :attr:`GeneFacts.known` is the flag a caller uses to grey out a control.
records.label: spacr.gene_facts#5

records.context: 3.  Groups are derived from the table. records.context: 4.  Loading can be done off the main GUI execution path. The first call reads five bundled CSVs (360 ms) and the first :attr:`GeneFacts.segments` reads DeepTMHMM's 8,140 rows. :func:`warm` does both in advance and joins the application view's terms in one pass: `annotate` re-checks all five right-hand structured-data names for uniqueness on every call, so one gene costs 20 ms and four hundred cost 21. records.context: Ordinary lasso penalises each guide on its own, so from a gene's four correlated guides it keeps whichever one happens to fit best and drops the rest -- which reads as "one guide works and three do not" when the four guides are four measurements of the same gene. Group lasso penalises the gene's guides as a block:
records.label: spacr.group_lasso#2
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: Ordinary lasso penalises each guide on its own, so from a gene's four correlated guides it keeps whichever one happens to fit best and drops the rest -- which reads as "one guide works and three do not" when the four guides are four measurements of the same gene. Group lasso penalises the gene's guides as a block:
records.translation: El lasso ordinario penaliza cada guía por separado, de modo que de las cuatro guías correlacionadas de un gen conserva la que casualmente ajusta mejor y descarta el resto, lo que se interpreta como "one guide works and three do not" cuando las cuatro guías son cuatro mediciones del mismo gen. El lasso por grupos penaliza las guías del gen como un bloque:

records.context: minimise  ||y - Xb||^2 / (2n)  +  lambda * sum_g sqrt(p_g) * ||b_g||_2
records.label: spacr.group_lasso#3
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: minimise  ||y - Xb||^2 / (2n)  +  lambda * sum_g sqrt(p_g) * ||b_g||_2
records.translation: minimizar  ||y - Xb||^2 / (2n)  +  lambda * sum_g sqrt(p_g) * ||b_g||_2

records.context: The L2 norm inside the sum is not squared, so its subgradient at zero is a ball rather than a point, and the whole block goes to exactly zero or none of it does. sqrt(p_g) is the standard correction that stops a gene with six guides being penalised more than one with three purely for having more.
records.label: spacr.group_lasso#4
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: The L2 norm inside the sum is not squared, so its subgradient at zero is a ball rather than a point, and the whole block goes to exactly zero or none of it does. sqrt(p_g) is the standard correction that stops a gene with six guides being penalised more than one with three purely for having more.
records.translation: La norma L2 dentro de la suma no está al cuadrado, de modo que su subgradiente en cero es una bola y no un punto, y el bloque entero pasa a ser exactamente cero o no lo pasa ninguna parte. sqrt(p_g) es la corrección estándar que impide que un gen con seis guías se penalice más que uno con tres solo por tener más.

records.context: For a CRISPR screening experiment it is the penalised analogue of the mixed model with random effects -- "which genes are involved, where each gene is measured by several guides" -- and it addresses that question with no random effects, no REML fit, and no `gene_fraction` column. `gene_fraction` is the sum of a gene's guide fractions, so a design carrying both blocks is singular by construction. Here the gene enters as a grouping of the guide columns, never as a column of its own, so the design stays full rank.
records.label: spacr.group_lasso#5
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: For a CRISPR screen it is the penalised analogue of the mixed model with random effects -- "which genes are involved, where each gene is measured by several guides" -- and it addresses that question with no random effects, no REML fit, and no `gene_fraction` column. `gene_fraction` is the sum of a gene's guide fractions, so a design carrying both blocks is singular by construction. Here the gene enters as a grouping of the guide columns, never as a column of its own, so the design stays full rank.
records.translation: Para un cribado CRISPR, es el análogo penalizado del modelo mixto con efectos aleatorios ("which genes are involved, where each gene is measured by several guides"), y aborda esa pregunta sin efectos aleatorios, sin ajuste REML y sin columna `gene_fraction`. `gene_fraction` es la suma de las fracciones de las guías de un gen, de modo que un diseño que lleve ambos bloques es singular por construcción. Aquí el gen entra como agrupación de las columnas de guías, nunca como una columna propia, de modo que el diseño mantiene el rango completo.

records.context: It also fits where OLS is undefined. This screen is 610 microplate sample positions and 823 guides; the penalty is what makes the answer well posed at p > n. A penalised fit therefore rests on the assumption that most guides have no effect; the penalty adds no new information.
records.label: spacr.group_lasso#6
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: It also fits where OLS is undefined. This screen is 610 wells and 823 guides; the penalty is what makes the answer well posed at p > n. A penalised fit therefore rests on the assumption that most guides have no effect; the penalty adds no new information.
records.translation: También ajusta donde OLS no está definido. Este cribado tiene 610 pocillos y 823 guías; la penalización es lo que hace que la respuesta esté bien planteada con p > n. Por tanto, un ajuste penalizado se basa en el supuesto de que la mayoría de las guías no tienen efecto; la penalización no añade información nueva.

records.context: The model gives no P value. A penalised coefficient's sampling distribution is not the OLS one, and a naive P value from it is biased toward significance. :func:`stability_selection` instead re-fits on many subsamples and reports the fraction of them in which a gene is selected, an error-controlled statement (Meinshausen & Buhlmann) that needs no distributional assumption.

records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: The model gives no P value. A penalised coefficient's sampling distribution is not the OLS one, and a naive P value from it is biased toward significance. :func:`stability_selection` instead re-fits on many subsamples and reports the fraction of them in which a gene is selected, an error-controlled statement (Meinshausen & Buhlmann) that needs no distributional assumption.

records.context: Rules that protect the annotations
records.label: spacr.suggest#3
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: Rules that protect the annotations
records.translation: Reglas que protegen las anotaciones

records.context: 1. A suggestion is never confusable with a decision. Suggestions are stored as their own values -- a suggested 1 becomes 11 -- so nothing that reads the annotation column can mistake one for a human's answer, and a processing session that goes wrong is undone by deleting a value rather than by remembering which rows were touched. 2. A suggestion never overwrites an annotation. Writes carry ``IS NULL``. Not when the model is confident, not on a repeat execution. A human's labels are the ground truth the model was fitted on; losing one silently would cost hours and would not be noticed until a processing session came out wrong. 3. There is no confidence floor; the order carries the uncertainty. Every unannotated extracted image region gets a suggestion, sorted most-confident first, and the reviewer stops where they stop agreeing. A threshold would make that decision with an arbitrary number. 4. A judgement is recorded, not inferred. Confirming a suggestion turns it into an ordinary label and rejecting one clears it -- and both are written down beside the column, in ``<column>_verdict``, as the class that was confirmed (``+c``) or rejected (``-c``). A rejection is information the next round can train on -- "not class 1" is an example of class 2 in a two-class column -- whereas a NULL would record nothing. The verdict column is added the first time a source is opened, so tables made before it existed gain it without a migration step.

A threshold would make that decision with an arbitrary number. 4. A judgement is recorded, not inferred. records.translation: 1. Una sugerencia nunca puede confundirse con una decisión. Las sugerencias se almacenan como valores propios (un 1 sugerido pasa a ser 11), de modo que nada que lea la columna de anotación puede tomar una por la respuesta de una persona, y una ejecución que sale mal se deshace eliminando un valor en lugar de recordando qué filas se tocaron. 2. Una sugerencia nunca sobrescribe una anotación. Las escrituras llevan ``IS NULL``. Ni cuando el modelo está seguro, ni en una nueva ejecución. Las etiquetas de una persona son la verdad de referencia con la que se ajustó el modelo; perder una en silencio costaría horas y no se notaría hasta que una ejecución saliera mal. 3. No hay un mínimo de confianza; el orden refleja la incertidumbre. Cada recorte sin anotar recibe una sugerencia, ordenada empezando por la más segura, y el revisor se detiene donde deja de estar de acuerdo. Un umbral tomaría esa decisión con un número arbitrario. 4. Un juicio se registra, no se deduce. Confirmar una sugerencia la convierte en una etiqueta normal y rechazarla la borra, y ambas cosas se anotan junto a la columna, en ``<column>_verdict``, como la clase que se confirmó (``+c``) o se rechazó (``-c``). Un rechazo es información con la que puede entrenar la ronda siguiente ("not class 1" es un ejemplo de la clase 2 en una columna de dos clases), mientras que un NULL no registraría nada. La columna de veredicto se añade la primera vez que se abre un origen, de modo que las tablas creadas antes de que existiera la obtienen sin un paso de migración.
